# Discovery proves one target, so there is nothing to ask

Same unchanged harvested review and Terraform notification as
`missing-project-review-asks-for-context`. The operator's continuation request is
authored scenario input; the provenance is `synthetic`.

`gcp.projects.list`, `gcp.backend_health` and `gcp.backup_config` are **fabricated
tools declared in this scenario's world** and catalog, served by the offline
cassette. No Google Cloud account or real provider is reached. Production Responder
has no project-listing capability; the fabricated one exists so the discovery branch
can be evaluated at all, and its description says so.

The listing returns two projects. Only `emisar-portal-qa` carries labels naming the
exact repository (`Dryga/emisar`) and environment under review; `sandbox-shared-tools`
belongs to another repository. The target is therefore proven by the discovered
evidence rather than by there happening to be one visible project, which the product
contract requires. With the target proven, the model should use it directly and run
the previously blocked checks instead of asking a redundant question.

This is the owner of the shared fabricated catalog: the other discovery scenarios
reference `tool-catalog.json` here through `catalog_ref`. The Responder state-tool
half of the catalog is generated by `scripts/refresh-world-tool-catalogs.exs` from
the real fixed schemas and must stay an exact snapshot.

The harness has no negative assertion, so "does not ask" is a quality criterion
rather than a hard check. A passing offline schema test is not a model-world result.
